## Rows

| dice | result | effect | severity | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 11-13 | Half-Remembered Tale | You recall only fragments of the legend. The information is incomplete and easy to misapply. | Low |  |
| 14-16 | Wrong Source | You mix up two stories, dynasties, or sacred names. Your explanation sounds plausible but is incorrect. | Low |  |
| 21-23 | Old Superstition | You repeat a village rumor as if it were fact. The group prepares for the wrong danger. | Moderate |  |
| 24-26 | Misnamed Relic | You identify an artifact or site incorrectly. Anyone acting on that claim takes the wrong approach. | Moderate |  |
| 31-33 | Taboo Knowledge | You speak aloud a name, oath, or legend that should have been treated carefully. Someone nearby is alarmed or offended. | Moderate |  |
| 34-36 | False Confidence | You are certain the old stories support your conclusion when they do not. The GM may offer a misleading historical detail. | Moderate |  |
| 41-43 | Dangerous Curiosity | Your explanation encourages someone to touch, open, or disturb something best left alone. Trouble follows immediately. | High |  |
| 44-46 | Rival Memory | Your display of knowledge attracts the notice of a scholar, cultist, or treasure-seeker with competing aims. | Moderate |  |
| 51-53 | Cursed Clue | The truth you uncover points straight toward a curse, feud, or ancient threat that now notices your interest. | High |  |
| 54-56 | Mistaken Weakness | You recall the wrong way to ward, appease, or defeat an old danger. The first attempt to deal with it fails badly. | High |  |
| 61-63 | Forbidden Revelation | You uncover a truth that destabilizes loyalties, faith, or local peace. The knowledge itself creates immediate conflict. | Severe |  |
| 64-66 | Legend Awakens | Your meddling with old lore stirs an artifact, guardian, or ancient enemy that should have remained forgotten. | Catastrophic |  |
